title: Effect of exercise-diet manipulation on muscle glycogen and its subsequent utilization during performance
authors: Sherman WM, Costill DL, Fink WJ, Miller JM
population: Trained runners (the abstract states neither their number nor their sex)
findings: Three exercise-diet regimens were compared for muscle glycogen supercompensation and for the performance of a 20.9-km run: 3 days of a 15% carbohydrate diet then 3 days of 70% (trial A), 3 days of 50% then 3 days of 70% (trial B), and 6 days of 50% (trial C).
Each trial used a 5-day depletion-taper exercise sequence on the treadmill at 73% of VO2max, with runs of 90, 40, 40, 20 and 20 min; a day of rest preceded the 20.9-km performance run.
Muscle glycogen of the gastrocnemius rose to 207, 203 and 159 mmol glucosyl units per kg wet tissue in trials A, B and C.

The performance run used more glycogen after trials A and B (5.0 and 5.1 mmol per km) than after trial C (3.1 mmol per km), but run times and post-run glycogen did not differ between the trials; the authors conclude that carbohydrate loading was of no benefit to trained runners over 20.9 km.
limitations: The abstract gives neither the number of runners nor their sex; the abstract gives no run time, and the performance run of 20.9 km is about a half marathon (any duration is an inference, not a finding); the diet and the exercise sequence were changed together, so the running of the last days is not tested apart from the diet; no study arm compares a run on the day before the performance run with a rest day.
implications: The nearest protocol in the corpus to a shake-out (inference): the last two runs before the performance run were 20 min at 73% of VO2max and the day before it was a rest day. It tested the diet and not the running of the last days.

A raised glycogen store did not shorten a 20.9-km run in trained runners, so the carbohydrate guidance of the final days is a statement about glycogen and long races and never a promise of time (inference).
No numeric taper parameter is justified from this study alone.

verification.notes: Added 2026-11-01 for task RF3 (the last two days before a long race, rule K6). Crossref: Int J Sports Med, May 1981, Sherman first author, four authors, no updated-by notice.
